name: OpenIndiana
summary: A community-driven, general-purpose Unix operating system distribution continuing the OpenSolaris legacy, built upon the illumos core consolidation and featuring the MATE desktop, IPS network packaging, and ZFS boot environments.

content.introduction: OpenIndiana is a free, open-source Unix operating system founded in September 2010 by the illumos community. Established as the direct open-source successor to the historic OpenSolaris operating system (project Indiana) following Sun Microsystems' acquisition by Oracle Corporation, OpenIndiana delivers a complete, installable system integrating the illumos kernel with a traditional desktop environment and modern software suites.
content.what_is_it: OpenIndiana is a full, turnkey operating system distribution that packages the foundational illumos-gate core (SunOS 5.11 kernel, OpenZFS, DTrace, Zones, SMF) into installable ISO media. It provides a familiar MATE desktop environment, text-mode server installers, and a complete open-source application stack managed via the network-centric Image Packaging System (IPS).
content.origin_and_opensolaris_continuity: When Oracle discontinued OpenSolaris in 2010, the community organized under the illumos project umbrella to maintain open-source Solaris computing. OpenIndiana was launched as the flagship distribution intended to preserve the OpenSolaris user experience, maintaining continuity for system administrators, developers, and researchers familiar with Sun Microsystems' enterprise workflows and administrative tools.
content.desktop_environment_and_tooling: OpenIndiana Hipster provides a complete graphical desktop environment built around MATE, preserving the classic Unix workstation paradigm originally popularized by the Java Desktop System and GNOME 2 on Solaris. The desktop is closely integrated with illumos storage features, notably through Time Slider, a graphical snapshot management applet integrated into the Caja file manager that enables users to browse, compare, and restore historical ZFS directory snapshots effortlessly. Audio output is managed through Boomer, the native Open Sound System (OSSv4) subsystem embedded in the illumos kernel, while graphical display services are powered by the X.Org server with open-source drivers for Intel and AMD GPUs. Automated network profile management is supported by Network Auto-Magic (NWAM), enabling seamless transitions between Ethernet and wireless interfaces.
content.package_management_and_boot_environments: Software management in OpenIndiana relies on the Image Packaging System (IPS), operated primarily through the command-line utility `pkg`. IPS is an enterprise-grade, network-native package manager that treats software updates as transactional operations. Software packages are published to network repositories known as publishers (with `openindiana.org` as the primary publisher). When system updates or kernel upgrades are performed, IPS automatically provisions a new OpenZFS boot environment using the `beadm` utility before applying changes. The existing operating system environment remains untouched, and the newly updated environment is activated upon reboot. If an upgrade encounters issues, users can instantly revert to previous boot environments via the GRUB boot menu.
content.release_model_and_platforms: OpenIndiana follows a continuous rolling-release distribution model under the project name OpenIndiana Hipster. Software packages, security patches, and kernel enhancements tracking upstream illumos-gate are continuously built and made available via the Hipster package publisher. Periodically, the project generates updated installation media (providing both Live GUI desktop images and minimal text-mode server installers) targeted exclusively at 64-bit x86-64 hardware platforms. OpenIndiana serves as an accessible bridge for developers, administrators, and enthusiasts wishing to explore illumos, DTrace, and OpenZFS within an interactive workstation environment.
content.installers_and_hardware_requirements: The official documentation describes two installation media: a live installer intended for workstations and a text installer intended for servers. Recommended specifications are a 64-bit processor, at least 20 GB of disk space and 2 GB of RAM, with 4 GB or more advised for desktop use; the default swap file is sized at 50% of installed memory, bounded between 512 MB and 32 GB. Snapshots of the Hipster branch are published roughly every six months, and the legacy oi-dev-151x branch is no longer maintained — the documentation recommends a clean install over an in-place upgrade from that branch.
content.security_maintenance_and_platform_scope: OpenIndiana states that it seeks to mitigate all known flaws quickly on the maintained Hipster branch, relying on user-submitted tickets in the project bug tracker, and it publishes no fixed support period per snapshot; the documentation warns that Hipster is a rapid development branch where caution is warranted in mission-critical production. On platform scope, the project FAQ states that Hipster is not currently available on SPARC and points to other illumos distributions (DilOS, OpenSXCE, Tribblix) and to commercial Oracle Solaris for SPARC hardware. The 2026-04 snapshot announcement referenced by this entry reports SPARC porting work; the two project sources diverge and the current status is left unresolved here.
advantages: Direct open-source successor to OpenSolaris, preserving familiar administrative tools and SunOS workflows
Native OpenZFS file system coupled with automated IPS boot environments (beadm) for risk-free upgrades
Full access to enterprise illumos technologies including DTrace, Solaris Zones, Crossbow, and SMF
Traditional, lightweight MATE desktop environment suitable for workstations and developer machines
Active rolling-release delivery model with periodic verified installation snapshots
disadvantages: Third-party desktop software catalog and hardware drivers (modern Wi-Fi, graphics GPUs) lag far behind Linux
Niche user base with fewer pre-built desktop applications and consumer multimedia tools
Requires familiarity with Solaris-specific paradigms such as IPS packaging, SMF manifests, and Zones
who_is_it_for: Unix administrators, systems programmers, and developers maintaining Solaris and SunOS environments
Storage administrators leveraging native OpenZFS, NFS services, and Crossbow network virtualization
Researchers and open-source enthusiasts studying illumos kernel architecture and DTrace observability
who_is_it_not_for: Mainstream desktop users requiring automated proprietary gaming clients, Steam Proton, and Bluetooth tooling
Users looking for extensive Linux binary package repositories (such as Debian apt or Fedora rpm)
content.verdict: OpenIndiana is a desktop- and workstation-oriented distribution of the illumos ecosystem. By pairing the SunOS kernel and OpenZFS with the Image Packaging System and a MATE desktop, it continues the OpenSolaris codebase on illumos.
content.community_hardware_compatibility_list:
The project maintains a community hardware compatibility list, published in its documentation as a page named Systems and organised in three tables: laptops, workstations and servers. Each row gives the manufacturer, the model, whether the system works (yes or no), notes or specific usage instructions, and the contributor who reported the entry. The list is contributed by users rather than issued by a certification programme, and a failing entry stays visible with its symptom instead of being removed.

The laptop table, consulted on 2026-10-18, includes the Acer Aspire One ZG8 reported as working, the Acer Aspire AS3810T reported as not working because it hangs after the operating system banner when booting from a USB DVD, the Dell Latitude D420 reported as not working, and the HP EliteBook 2170p reported as not working with the hipster-20190308 image because wireless does not work, with a reference to the bug report. The same page lists, among servers, the HP ProLiant Microserver N40L and the SuperMicro SuperServer 6016T-MTHF as working without special drivers, and the Zotac Zbox ID-18U as working except for Intel graphics, limited to VGA, and USB 3, for which no driver is available.

The page metadata gives a creation date of 2019-07-29 and a last update of 2026-05-24, which situates the list in time and dates its most recent revision.

components.name: illumos-gate
components.note: "illumos-gate includes the illumos kernel, along with many of the device drivers, core libraries, and system utilities"; "To form a complete distribution, the OpenIndiana project combines illumos-gate with oi-userland, and with other free and open-source software" (About OpenIndiana, docs.openindiana.org/misc/openindiana/).

components.name: oi-userland
components.note: "To form a complete distribution, the OpenIndiana project combines illumos-gate with oi-userland, and with other free and open-source software"; the documentation carries a "Building with oi-userland" section (About OpenIndiana).

components.name: IPS
components.note: "OpenIndiana uses the network based Image Packaging System (IPS)"; "You may also continue to use the legacy pkgadd/pkgrm commands" (About OpenIndiana, "What package manager does OpenIndiana use?").

components.name: MATE
components.note: "By default, the windowing GUI system is based on the popular Mate system" (About OpenIndiana); the handbook table gives "Live installer (Mate desktop)" and documents "pkg install mate_install", and the 2026.04 announcement lists a "Mate desktop 1.28 refresh". The release-schedule table on the same About page lists the live installer as "(Gnome desktop)".

relations.name: illumos
relations.note: Upstream core operating system consolidation and kernel upon which OpenIndiana is built.

relations.name: FreeBSD
relations.note: Fellow open-source Unix-like operating system sharing OpenZFS and enterprise reliability, comparing SunOS/illumos with BSD.

relations.name: GhostBSD
relations.note: Fellow user-friendly Unix-like desktop system featuring the MATE desktop and native ZFS boot environments.

variants.name: OpenIndiana Hipster 2026.04 (snapshot)
variants.description: Current Hipster snapshot, published as Live DVD, Live USB, Text Install and Minimal Install images for 64-bit x86 and announced on 5 May 2026; the About page states that the project "releases a snapshot of the Hipster rolling release branch" approximately every six months.

variants.name: oi-dev-151x (legacy branch)
variants.description: The About page states that "the legacy oi-dev-151x branch is no longer maintained"; upgrades to Hipster remain possible, with a clean install described as the most trouble-free method.
